widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1>: The target person in <Picture 1>, defining their face, hair, clothing, materials, proportions and worn accessories.
<Subject 2>: The central source performer originally wearing a pale suit in <Video 1>, whose appearance is replaced by <Subject 1>.
<Video 1>: The source performance, defining each person's movements, expressions, interactions, visibility, camera, environment and timing.

summary:
[video editing + reference generation] Edit <Video 1> by replacing exactly one existing person: <Subject 2> with <Subject 1>. Preserve every other person's original appearance and the source performance.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1>: fully_preserved — preserve the identity and visible appearance defined by <Picture 1>, including clothing materials and the presence or absence of worn accessories, throughout the clip.
<Subject 2>: attribute_transfer — transfer only this source person's pose, actions, expressions, position and visibility to <Subject 1>; replace their face, hair, clothing and worn accessories.
<Video 1>: partially_preserved — retain the source number of people, unassigned people's original appearances, interactions, handheld props, scene, lighting, camera, existing cuts and timing.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1] The central performer <Subject 2> becomes <Subject 1>, using only the appearance in <Picture 1>. Follow this source person's actions and expressions once in the original order and speed. Adapt the movement naturally to the target person's proportions while preserving the source interactions and timing.

Exactly one source-person track is replaced. The identity in <Picture 1> belongs only to the selected central performer. Every other person retains their own original face, hair, clothing and worn accessories, including during proximity, overlap and occlusion. Do not duplicate or blend the target identity, or transfer appearance features between people.

Track the selected performer through turns, crossings, occlusions and existing source cuts. Their assignment stays fixed when their screen position changes. When they leave the view, the replacement leaves with them; when they reappear, retain the same target identity and outfit. Render only the people visible in the source at each moment. Reference pictures supply appearance only; preserve the source environment, lighting, perspective, contact, shadows, handheld props and camera. Do not add actions, people or cuts, loop the opening, or revert to the original performer's appearance.

overall_soundscape:
Reference the timing and environmental sound characteristics of <Video 1>. Do not add dialogue or unrelated sound effects. Exact source soundtrack preservation requires separate audio handling.

non_diegetic_music:
Reference any existing music in <Video 1>; do not introduce unrelated music.

nodes.title: Character Replacement Guide
widgets_values:
1. Replace the character image and source video.
2. Update the prompt to identify exactly one source person to replace; Picture 1 defines their new appearance.
3. Set mode, service, LoRA, width, height and fps in Global Control.
4. Run and check the saved preview.

widgets_values_named.text:
1. Enable the case you want to run; mute the others.
2. Replace its character images and source video(s).
3. Update the prompt to say which source person each picture replaces. Keep the existing prompt structure.
4. In Global Control, set mode, service URL, model, LoRA paths, width, height and fps.
5. Run and check the preview.

Case03: when changing source clips, update each segment's prompt, duration and guide/trim frames. Its current frame settings use 24 FPS.
